title: Blockwise Online-Softmax Attention
prompt:
Implement `blockwise_attention(Q, K, V, block_size)` with PyTorch, a single-head simulation of `softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d)) @ V`. Inputs are finite 2D float32/float64 tensors with matching dtype/device: Q `(nq, d)`, K `(nk, d)`, V `(nk, dv)`; all dimensions are positive and scaled dot products are representable. Array-like inputs may be converted with `torch.as_tensor` (non-floating inputs use the default floating dtype). `block_size` is a positive Python integer and may exceed either input dimension. Return a finite tensor `(nq, dv)`, preserving dtype, device, and gradients to Q/K/V without mutating inputs.

Tile both query rows and key/value columns in chunks no larger than `block_size`. Merge per-row running maximum, softmax denominator, and weighted-value numerator with stable online-softmax rescaling. Only score tiles of at most `block_size × block_size` may be computed; do not materialize a full attention matrix as a separate intermediate or call SDPA/FlashAttention or another attention helper. Every positive tile size must match stable dense attention within floating-point tolerance, including gradients. Autograd may save tiles for backward; implementing a custom memory-efficient backward or GPU kernel is not required. No mask is part of this exercise.

Reject invalid ranks, empty/incompatible shapes, dtype/device mismatches, and invalid tile sizes with `ValueError` or `AssertionError`. The API and shapes are local practice choices; the report identifies a FlashAttention implementation task and a basic-simulation interpretation.
